title: Ludwik Wąsowicz to Aleksander Michał Lubomirski, seven cipher letters of 1662-1663 (catalogue 439): simple number substitution on Polish, key sheet R7501

steps.what: Table rebuilt from the key sheet R7501.
Blind check: R7508 transcribed and frozen before decoding, then read with the R7501 table.
Seven letters read in Polish with English translation; R7510 redated 1663 and joined to R7509.

PR review on merge (Claude Opus 5.5 for Daniel Bourdeau): the key sheet R7501 credited; the credit for the images sent for study removed (the project is not credited in its own profiles; the thanks stay in NOTES.md).

Claude Opus 5.5 (PR review on merge): shelfmark (Krzeszowickie, not Krakowskie), system (simple substitution, not homophonic), gaps, fraction_read measured over all eight letters (0.984), token counts (numbers only), summaries and routes corrected; every letter graded A.

outcome.method_basis: Key sheet R7501 in the same file, transcribed and checked blind on R7508.
outcome.fraction_read_source: All eight transcriptions, numbers only (page labels and separators left out): 1,561 of 1,587 numbers transcribed without doubt and in the table; per letter 13/13, 163/164, 113/113, 173/174, 162/166, 219/234, 27/27, 691/696. Measured on review, 27 Oct 2026.

credits.note: seven letters read with the R7501 table; Polish texts and English translations; R7510 redated
DECODE R7501, the nineteenth-century table 'Klucz Wąsowicza (i Kotowicza) do Alex. Lubomirskiego' in the same file (AKPot 3227 p. 81), applied as the key

texts.label: Wąsowicz to Lubomirski, 29 November 1662 (ANK AKPot 3227, p. 137; DECODE R7503)
texts.summary: Wąsowicz reports that the Voivode of Ruthenia, Stefan Czarniecki, has himself subscribed to something; only his title is in cipher. Written as the Crown army's confederation pressed the court for its pay.

reading_review.note: Read as Polish sentences against the English translation: coherent throughout with scattered marked holes.

texts.label: Wąsowicz to Lubomirski, [December 1662 – January 1663] (undated) (ANK AKPot 3227, pp. 181–183; DECODE R7504)
texts.summary: Undated letter of winter 1662-1663: the Marshal Jerzy Sebastian Lubomirski leaves for the army's circle at Wolbórz; the rest concerns the estate of Błażejowa, held in pledge for 300,000 by a Tekieli who lacked indigenate, and how to secure a donation of it on the palatine's death. The names are in cipher.

reading_review.note: Read as Polish sentences against the English translation: coherent throughout with scattered marked holes.

texts.label: Wąsowicz to Lubomirski, 25 January 1663 (ANK AKPot 3227, p. 200; DECODE R7505)
texts.summary: The court strives to keep the agreement with the confederated army; the circle of Wolbórz must be satisfied, and the whole point is that the money be brought in. Wąsowicz watches the Marshal's manoeuvres.

reading_review.note: Read as Polish sentences against the English translation: coherent throughout with scattered marked holes.

texts.label: Wąsowicz to Lubomirski, 17–18 February 1663 (ANK AKPot 3227, p. 209; DECODE R7506)
texts.summary: The Marshal is well received by the King and Queen at the audiences; someone was told to negotiate nothing further, only to serve the King after the confederation and to watch whether the army plots harm against the fatherland.

reading_review.note: Read as Polish sentences against the English translation: coherent throughout with scattered marked holes.

texts.label: Wąsowicz to Lubomirski, 19 March 1663 (ANK AKPot 3227, p. 225; DECODE R7507)
texts.summary: The Marshal has obliged the royal couple by sending Tatar [prisoners?]; he will not detach the better banners from the confederation before the circle, but promises that many will leave it afterwards; Czarniecki will not set out again.

reading_review.note: Read as Polish sentences against the English translation: coherent throughout with scattered marked holes. The last clause of R7507 (‹przezęidą›) does not form a sentence.

texts.label: Wąsowicz to Lubomirski, 5 May 1663 (ANK AKPot 3227, p. 235; DECODE R7508)
texts.summary: The Marshal stays at Łańcut without a word to the court; when the King moves from Cracow with the camp, the plan is to see whether the Marshal detaches the banners from the confederation as he promised and brings them to the King.

reading_review.note: Read as Polish sentences against the English translation: coherent throughout with scattered marked holes.

texts.label: Wąsowicz to Lubomirski, 9 December 1663 (ANK AKPot 3227, p. 239; DECODE R7509)
texts.summary: Beginning of the letter of 9 December 1663, continued in R7510: the Archdeacon of Sandomierz has not asked after Lubomirski's health.

reading_review.note: Read as Polish sentences against the English translation: coherent throughout with scattered marked holes.

texts.label: Wąsowicz to Lubomirski, 9 December 1663, continued (Jarosław) (ANK AKPot 3227, pp. 245–248; DECODE R7510)
texts.summary: End of the Jarosław letter of 9 December 1663, after the funeral of the Cupbearer (probably Konstanty Jacek Lubomirski): Born's grievances and his taking of Połonne; the Marshal refuses the King's Ukrainian campaign ('iam ani hetman ani żołnierz do wiosny'); the army's deputies paid in debased szelągi; gossip about the Cupbearer's death.

reading_review.note: Read as Polish sentences against the English translation: coherent throughout with scattered marked holes.

outcome.notes: R7502 (about Sept 1662) is deciphered at the time between the lines and on the nineteenth-century sheet R7511; both are outside this target and not repeated here.
